title: Understanding the 2024 US presidential election
lede: Who won, how the Electoral College turns state results into a president, and what two years of the second Trump term have meant at home and abroad. As of 10 November 2026.

stats.l: electoral votes for Donald Trump (270 wins)

visual_note: Donald Trump won about 77.3 million votes to Kamala Harris's 75.0 million, roughly 50% to 48%. The map gives each hexagon one electoral vote.
elects: The president and vice president, for four years from 20 January 2025. Donald Trump, who had been president from 2017 to 2021, returned for a second, non-consecutive term with JD Vance as vice president.

The same day also elected all 435 House members and a third of the Senate. Republicans held the House narrowly and took the Senate, so the White House and Congress were under one party for the first two years.

system.oneline: Voters choose electors, not the president directly. A candidate needs 270 of 538 electoral votes.

steps.p: A state has as many electoral votes as it has House seats plus two Senate seats. DC has three. That is the number of hexagons each state gets on this map.
In 48 states and DC, whoever wins the state's popular vote takes all its electoral votes. Maine and Nebraska split theirs by congressional district.

steps.h: Small states count extra, swing states count most
steps.p: Every state's two Senate-based electors make small states weigh more per person, and because most states are one-sided, campaigns concentrate on a handful of close ones.
It is possible to win more votes nationally and lose the Electoral College, as happened in 2000 and 2016. In 2024 the winner led both.

home: Republican control of both chambers let the administration move quickly on tax, immigration and federal agencies for two years. Foreign aid was reshaped, with the administration moving to dissolve USAID and shift Food for Peace to the Agriculture Department.

home.p: In the November 2026 midterms, voters concerned about affordability and perceived corruption gave Democrats control of both chambers. That makes the 2024 result the high-water mark of a unified government. See the midterms maps for the county-level detail.

world.p: Tariffs became the hallmark of Trump's foreign policy in his first year back, used to press countries on trade and on politics. A 50% rate on Brazilian goods in 2025 is the sharpest example.
The administration cut aid to Ukraine sharply, spoke of leaving NATO, and criticised many allies. Congress has already required a baseline of 76,000 US troops in Europe.
By 2026 the US was in a war with Iran and striking suspected drug boats off South America. On 3 January 2026 US forces struck Venezuela and captured its president, Nicolás Maduro.

p: Republicans won both chambers in 2024, so a Harris administration would have faced a hostile Congress from day one and little room to pass its agenda. Its main power would have been executive action and appointments.

Abroad, Democratic priorities, as Foreign Policy summarised them after the midterms, include closer NATO ties, more support for Ukraine and restraint on boat strikes in Latin America. Tariffs would probably have been less central to foreign policy, though Democrats have also toughened their stance on China.
